collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult; in the story (name1) has a long-term breathing condition)

collection.description: Bonfire smoke at the festival has a villager with a breathing condition wheezing: move the fun upwind, or sit away from it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has had trouble breathing for most of (subject.his/her) life. On ordinary days it's fine. But tonight is the festival, with three big bonfires, and the smoke is already rolling across the clearing. (subject) has started to wheeze. (friend) has noticed (subject.him/her) sitting off to one side, very still, concentrating on each breath.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (friend) gets a few people to help carry the drums and food baskets to the other side of the fires, where the wind blows the smoke away. Nobody asks why. The party moves. (subject)'s breathing slowly eases. (subject.He/she) spends the rest of the night upwind, dancing badly and happily. Next year, the festival is set up that way from the start.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (friend) brings (subject) a cup of the steamy herb tea the healers make, and sits with (subject.him/her) at the edge of the trees, away from the smoke. They can still hear the music. It's not the festival (subject) wanted. It's still a good evening. They talk about everything and nothing until the fires burn low and the air clears.
